title: Eight shifts from AI Engineer New York 2026
summary: Across 31 recorded talks, 95,224 spoken words, and 176 transcript-verified claims, New York’s engineering rooms converged on one reckoning: generating code and prose is now cheap, so the real engineering work has moved into synthetic domain evals, sandboxed computers, deterministic verification gates, runtime risk governance, and self-improving agent fleets.
share_text: Enjoyed your talk at AI Engineer NYC 2026

stack.title: How the eight shifts fit together
stack.lede: Select any layer to inspect its representative stage slide, its sharpest verbatim claim, and the talks that built or contested it.

cards.title: The eight conference themes
cards.lede: Each theme opens into an interactive scrollytelling deep dive backed by stage slides, counter-claims, and verbatim transcript evidence.

bootstrapping-domain-evals-without-publi.alt: Slide: So we wrote the answer first — reversing evaluation from weekly expert grading to picking a page, generating the question, and checking retrieval in code in seconds.
bootstrapping-domain-evals-without-publi.speaker: Nathanael Weill (Air Canada)

token-economics-right-sizing-and-open-fo.alt: Slide: Cost per accepted outcome = tokens × price ÷ outcomes someone actually used — cheap models that fail a third of the time cost more than dear ones that work.
token-economics-right-sizing-and-open-fo.speaker: Eugene Cheah (Featherless AI)

sandboxed-computers-context-architecture.alt: Slide: Frameworks agree on nothing. Except this. — across graphs, crews, and loops, every major agent framework ships a sandboxed computer primitive.
sandboxed-computers-context-architecture.speaker: Mislav Ivanda (Daytona)

bounded-autonomy-runtime-governance-and-.alt: Slide: How they fit together — Create a registry, Score differentiated risk, Run guardrails, Share evals and metrics, and Govern strong runtime protections.
bounded-autonomy-runtime-governance-and-.speaker: John Feminella (Two Sigma)

deterministic-verification-loops-over-li.alt: Slide: Coding is solved. Verification is not. — 85% of organizations use coding agents, 76% generate AI code faster than they can verify it, and 53% spend more time reviewing than writing.
deterministic-verification-loops-over-li.speaker: Manish Kapur & Addy Osmani (Sonar / Google Cloud)

self-improving-fleets-and-the-agent-mana.alt: Slide: Taking a deeper look within FleetKit — versioned protocol and domain-context repositories driving a Claude Code session coordinated with SMEs in a mission channel and war room.
self-improving-fleets-and-the-agent-mana.speaker: Ford Prior (Fable Security)

governed-ontologies-provenance-and-finan.alt: Slide: Coatue gather() for the Korean news — directed acyclic graph wiring news, DART filings, and call transcripts through quote extraction, source checks, entity linking, and human review.
governed-ontologies-provenance-and-finan.speaker: Frank Long (Coatue)

spatiotemporal-world-models-and-real-tim.alt: Slide: LLMs predict the next word, our models predict the next action — pre-training on millions of hours of action-labelled gameplay to operate games and robots in real time.
spatiotemporal-world-models-and-real-tim.speaker: Pim de Witte (General Intuition)
